newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Oxy eyes Colombia output boost, fears well problems.
newsitem.headline: Oxy eyes Colombia output boost, fears well problems.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp aims to ramp up output from its Cano Limon field in northeast Colombia once security problems are resolved but fears damage to wells could prevent the move, a spokesman said Wednesday.

Production at the Cano Limon field, the biggest oil find in the Western hemisphere, has been paralyzed since last Thursday after leftist rebels carried out a spate of dynamite attacks on the pipeline that pumps crude to the Caribbean coast port of Covenas.
"We have capacity to increase output by 75,000 barrels per day but everything depends on the state of the wells after the field reopens," the Occidental spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said the 44-inch diameter Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline was capable of pumping about 250,000 barrels per day in optimum conditions.
Earlier this week, the spokesman said the field shut-in could damage some of the 135 wells but said exact data would be unavailable until production restarted.

Occidental forecast production through 1997 would average 175,000 barrels per day. That target suffered a setback last month when back-to-back pipeline bombings forced the U.S. multinational to scale back production to 171,000 barrels per day.

When National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels paralyzed the pipeline again on July 6, Occidental slashed production to 70,000 barrels per day in view of its limited on-site crude storage capacity. A second attack within four days forced all production to be halted.
State-run oil company Ecopetrol estimated Cano Limon had lost two million barrels of output so far this year.

Engineers have been unable to repair the pipeline following the latest attack and hopes that teams would begin work later Wednesday appeared to be fading by mid-afternoon as heavy rains lashed the blast site in northeast Arauca province.
The Occidental spokesman conceded that even once the pipeline was back in action it could face further attacks, thereby dealing a further setback to the company's production targets.
